answer: Each epoch runs a capped admission auction: a candidate locks spendable funds and reveals a bid bound to its public key, plus a one-time marble nonce reserved on-ledger so one lock cannot back two reveals. Only the top S bids receive a slot; losers pay a non-refundable fee. Scarce slots form an oasis of limited identity supply, so a swarm must outbid honest demand for every sockpuppet and immobilize capital for M epochs. A won slot cannot be transferred, because the signed reveal is the only accepted bridge from the locked bid to standing; a forged reveal fails signature checks.
